skill.name: performance-optimization
skill.description: Optimize frontend, backend, query, and database performance. Use it to diagnose bottlenecks, improve Core Web Vitals, reduce latency, and prevent regressions.
skill.summary: Measure, improve, and verify application performance across frontend, backend, queries, and databases.
skill.author: addyosmani

content.value_statement: Performance problems are difficult to diagnose when teams optimize from assumptions. This skill provides a measurement-first workflow for finding bottlenecks, testing fixes, and preventing regressions.
actual_capabilities: Guide baseline measurement for Core Web Vitals, API latency, database queries, and bundle size.
Diagnose common frontend bottlenecks, including large bundles, layout shifts, slow interactions, and unnecessary renders.
Explain query-plan analysis, indexing decisions, N+1 query fixes, pagination, and connection-pool sizing.
Recommend cache layers, cache keys, expiration policies, and stampede protection based on data freshness needs.
Define verification steps, performance budgets, monitoring signals, and regression checks.
limitations: It cannot measure a live application without profiling data, test results, or representative measurements.
It provides guidance rather than automatically changing source code, infrastructure, or database schemas.
Recommendations depend on the application framework, database engine, traffic pattern, and deployment model.
Performance targets require validation on representative devices, networks, datasets, and production workloads.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a Slow Web Page
use_cases.description: Use measured browser data to identify bundle, rendering, image, interaction, or server-response bottlenecks.

use_cases.title: Tune Database-Backed APIs
use_cases.description: Review query plans, indexes, pagination, N+1 patterns, and connection pools before changing backend code.

use_cases.title: Set a Regression Guardrail
use_cases.description: Create performance budgets and monitoring checks that verify improvements and catch later regressions.

prompt_templates.title: Find the First Measurement
prompt_templates.prompt: My application feels slow. Ask for the minimum data needed, then identify the first measurements I should collect.

prompt_templates.title: Review Frontend Metrics
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these LCP, INP, CLS, bundle, and network results. Identify the most likely bottleneck and propose one testable fix.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Query Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this query and EXPLAIN ANALYZE output. Explain the bottleneck, evaluate index options, and state the measurement needed after the change.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Performance Experiment
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a controlled performance experiment for this suspected bottleneck. Define the baseline, one change, success threshold, variance check, rollback rule, and regression guard.

output_examples.input: The page has LCP of 4.2 seconds, a 1.8 MB JavaScript bundle, and large hero images.
output: Prioritize the hero image and initial JavaScript payload.
Measure image transfer, render blocking, and bundle composition.
Test responsive image formats and route-level code splitting.
Keep the change only if LCP improves beyond normal run-to-run variance.

output_examples.input: An API loads tasks and fetches each task owner separately.
output_examples.output: This is an N+1 query pattern. Fetch tasks with their owners in one query, then compare query count and p95 latency before and after.

output_examples.input: A cache serves user profiles by profile ID, but the response includes tenant-specific permissions.
output_examples.output: The cache key omits a response input. Include tenant and permission context, or avoid shared caching when authorization data must remain isolated.

best_practices: Measure a representative baseline before proposing an optimization.
Change one variable at a time and compare results against run-to-run variance.
Keep only changes that improve the target metric without reducing correctness.
anti_patterns: Adding indexes, caches, or memoization without evidence of a measured bottleneck.
Keeping a neutral optimization because it has already been implemented.
Combining several changes in one experiment so their effects cannot be attributed.

faq.question: What should I measure first?
faq.answer: Start with the user-visible symptom and collect a baseline for the relevant metric, such as LCP, INP, p95 latency, or query time.

faq.question: Can this skill optimize my code automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides analysis, recommendations, and verification steps. You decide which code, database, or infrastructure changes to implement.

faq.question: When should I add a database index?
faq.answer: Inspect the query plan first. Add an index when it addresses the query shape and measure both read improvement and write cost.

faq.question: How should I choose a cache?
faq.answer: Choose the smallest suitable layer based on scope, freshness, invalidation, and recomputation cost. Include every response input in the cache key.

faq.question: How do I know an optimization worked?
faq.answer: Repeat the baseline measurement under comparable conditions. Keep the change only when the improvement exceeds normal variance and tests remain correct.

faq.question: Does this cover production monitoring?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends synthetic budgets and field monitoring for the primary user-facing metric, with alerts that lead back to fresh measurement.
